title: Geometric irreducibility of the universal Bertini generic fibre
statement: Let $k$ be a field, $Y$ a scheme of finite type over $k$ which is geometrically irreducible over $k$, $\mathcal L$ an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module, $V$ a finite-dimensional $k$-vector space and $\psi:V\to\Gamma(Y,\mathcal L)$ a $k$-linear map. Assume (i) there are $v_1,v_2,v_3\in V$ and an irreducible component $W$ of $H_{v_2}\cap H_{v_3}$ with $W\not\subseteq H_{v_1}$ and $\operatorname{codim}(W,Y)=2$; (ii) every irreducible component $B$ of $\bigcap_{v\in V}H_v$ has $\operatorname{codim}(B,Y)\ge2$. For every basis b of V, the generic residue-field fibre of the universal incidence projection q of [def-zl-bertini-universal-family] is geometrically irreducible over the parameter generic residue field. Geometric irreducibility and the scheme-theoretic fibre use [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] and [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Conventions: schemes and their residue fields [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], finite type and quasi-compact morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], invertible modules [def-sc-invertible-module], section zero schemes [def-pc-zero-scheme].

proof.text: Obtain the affine data, irreducible incidence scheme, dominance and residue-field arrow isomorphism from the incidence chart presentation. Dominance sends its generic point to the parameter generic point.

Apply irreducibility of a dominant generic fibre. The fibre inclusion is an embedding, so the source generic point viewed in the fibre is generic there. The proved fibre residue-arrow isomorphism identifies its residue-field arrow with the original map on incidence residue fields.

The affine algebraic Bertini theorem proves geometric irreducibility of Omega over F. Transport through the two arrow isomorphisms and apply the generic-residue-field criterion to the irreducible generic fibre. Transport the resulting fibre property along the generic-point image equality.

theorem geometricallyIrreducible_bertiniUniversal_genericFiber
    (k : Type u) [Field k] (Y : Scheme.{u}) [Y.Over (Spec (.of k))]
    [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))] [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    [GeometricallyIrreducible (Y ↘ Spec (.of k))]
    (L : Y.Modules) [L.IsInvertible]
    (V : Type v) [AddCommGroup V] [Module k V] [FiniteDimensional k V] :
    letI : Module k Γ(L, ⊤) :=
      Module.compHom Γ(L, ⊤) (Scheme.globalSectionsRingHom k (X := Y))
    ∀ ψ : V →ₗ[k] Γ(L, ⊤),
      (∃ (v₁ v₂ v₃ : V) (W : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y),
        Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y ↦
          (Z : Set Y) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₂)).zeroLocus.support ∩
            (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₃)).zeroLocus.support) W ∧
        ¬ (W : Set Y) ⊆ (Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ v₁)).zeroLocus.support ∧
        Order.coheight W = 2) →
      (∀ B : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y,
        Maximal (fun Z : TopologicalSpace.IrreducibleCloseds Y ↦
          (Z : Set Y) ⊆ ⋂ w : V,
            ((Scheme.Modules.homOfGlobalSection L (ψ w)).zeroLocus.support : Set Y)) B →
        2 ≤ Order.coheight B) →
      ∀ (r : ℕ) (b : Module.Basis (Fin r) k V),
        GeometricallyIrreducible
          ((bertiniUniversalProjection (Y ↘ Spec (.of k)) L
            (fun i : ULift.{u} (Fin r) ↦ ψ (b i.down))).fiberToSpecResidueField
            (genericPoint (Spec (.of (MvPolynomial (ULift.{u} (Fin r)) k)))))
